newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Mar 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The 1997/98 budget that will straddle the territory's handover to China on July 1, announced by Financial Secretary Donald Tsang on Wednesday, was the top story in all papers.
-- MING PAO -- About 1.34 million people would benefit from the new budget, which lowered the salaries tax and increased tax allowances.

-- Beijing has given instructions to China's provinces to re-examine their work on minority groups and handle such issues with care in the wake of bombings in the mostly Moslem western Xinjiang region. Beijing also instructed that mosques be preserved.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Chinese side of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group handling Hong Kong's handover expressed regrets over the British side's failure to show up at a meeting concerning defence and public order.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The new budget stressed prudence and estimated a record surplus of HK$31.7 billion next year.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The property sector worried that speculation would be encouraged by the new budget, which cut stamp duty for properties worth HK$4 million or less and failed to supply enough new flats in the coming year.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Urban Council decided that commemoration of the massacre at Beijing's Tiananmen Square on July 4, 1989, could go ahead but refused the Democratic Party's request to hold a rally on the eve of the handover on June 30.

-- Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp, which ran the most profitable joint venture in China, was set to take controlling stakes in two poorly performing listed companies in a new wave of mergers and acquisitions.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- An early rush of buyers for new listing Shenzhen Expressway clogged the stock exchange processing system, causing a back-log in trade executions.
